name: Nattokinase
short: A single case report describes a brain haemorrhage in a patient taking nattokinase with aspirin. A meta-analysis of six trials (546 people) reported no notable adverse events.
text: A single case report describes a patient taking aspirin for secondary stroke prevention who had an acute cerebellar (brain) haemorrhage after taking nattokinase 400 mg daily for 7 days; brain imaging also showed multiple microbleeds, and the authors suggested that nattokinase may increase the risk of bleeding in the brain in people with bleeding-prone small-vessel disease who are also receiving another antithrombotic medicine. In a meta-analysis of six randomised trials (546 participants), no notable adverse events were reported due to nattokinase. In a real-life study of 153 patients with vascular diseases, some of whom also received the anticoagulants fondaparinux or enoxaparin, no adverse drug reactions or drug interactions were recorded.
